newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish rightist party attacks big privatisations.
newsitem.headline: Polish rightist party attacks big privatisations.

text.p: Poland's opposition Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland (ROP) party on Friday demanded that the government halt its privatisation of copper concern KGHM Polska Miedz SA, saying the sale was hugely underpriced.
The ROP also attacked the sale of Poland's biggest bank, Bank Handlowy SA, as a scandal.

"ROP demands a halt to the privatisation of KGHM by this (current) method," the radical rightist party's head Jan Olszewski told a news conference. "In our opinion the state treasury will lose about $2 billion on this privatisation."
ROP economic commentator Janusz Szewczak also savaged the sale of Bank Handlowy now underway. "The privatisation of Bank Handlowy SA is a scandal," he said.

"Instead of earning $3.5 billion...from foreign investors, the state budget has gained barely $200 million. All of this is due to the scandalously low price of 35 zloty a share," Szewczak told the news conference.
Handlowy's public offering closed this week heavily oversubscribed with the $200 million institutional tranche attracting more than $3.5 billion worth of foreign bids.

ROP, which in opinion polls shows just enough support to get into parliament, often expresses a sentiment common in Poland's wider rightist opposition that the government led by ex-communists is selling prize assets cheaply to foreigners.

The initial public offer of KGHM is due to start on June 30 and the treasury intends to sell up to 72 million shares. The state treasury earlier on Friday set the price range for institutional investors at 18 to 23 zlotys per share.
Szewczak said KGHM had been undervalued because the price was decided when the price of copper was lower than it is now. Investors have been offered 61.75 million shares in Handlowy.

Poland is to hold general elections on September 21 and a survey by the public CBOS polling agency published on Friday showed ROP with five percent support -- the bare minimum needed to enter parliament.

ROP is broadly aligned with the larger Solidarity Election Action (AWS), an opposition alliance of about 45 groups including some with similar views to ROP on the economy, and the two could form a coalition after the election.
According to the CBOS poll, AWS now has 21 percent support compared with 26 percent for the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) which is now in government along with a smaller Peasant party.

AWS has also been critical of the government's big-ticket privatisations this year, mainly because it says more of the proceeds should be used to provide capital for funds that would lay the basis for a reformed social security system.
